newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobs loot and burn Tutsi property in Zaire capital.
newsitem.headline: Mobs loot and burn Tutsi property in Zaire capital.

text.p: Angry mobs looted and burned property belonging to Tutsis in Zaire's capital Kinshasa at the weekend amid growing signs of a witchhunt in response to a Tutsi revolt in the east.
Ethnic Tutsis, who prior to the conflict featured prominently in Zaire's business and professional communities, are packing up and trying to leave the city.

As the mayor of Kinshasa made a radio appeal for calm in the local lingala language and said the authorities would crack down on looting, relatives and friends of Tutsis who went missing in the disturbances tried anxiously to trace them.

"We have had no news of Alexei or his family since Friday," said one friend of Alexei Gisaro, owner of one of the destroyed houses and the oldest son of the first Banyamulenge member of Zaire's parliament. The friend asked to remain anonymous.
The Banyamulenge, a community of about 300,000 Tutsis in the east, form the backbone of the revolt which the authorities in Kinshasa also blame on Tutsi-led Rwanda and Burundi.
Tutsis in Kinshasa are the latest victims of Hutu-Tutsi rivalry that has poisoned life in neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi for generations.
Hundreds have crossed the Zaire River from Kinshasa to Brazzaville, the capital of neighbouring Congo, since the rebel offensive began last month.
The campaign against them in the capital began with harassment but has escalated into attacks targeting Rwandan, Burundian or ethnic-Tutsi property .
Witnesses said two houses belonging to Tutsis were ransacked on Saturday and three cars parked outside burnt. Mobs attacked Tutsi-owned shops on Friday.
"The Zaireans attacked my home and now I have to live under cover. As soon as I can I will get out to Congo," said one Tutsi, until recently an administrator at a local factory.
Witnesses say a house belonging to Burundian embassy staff in the wealthy Binza neighbourhood of Kinshasa was ransacked on Saturday by student demonstrators.
Outside a pile of burnt objects including fridges, crockery and sofas smouldered on Sunday.
"There were hundreds of demonstrators. They went into the house and flung out all the contents before making a big bonfire," a cigarette seller who witnessed the scene said.
The eight staff inside, who included the embassy driver, happened to be Hutus. All escaped.
Many Rwandan students were in hiding inside their embassy on Sunday.

Zaire's part-Tutsi prime minister, Kengo wa Dongo, has become a target of anti-Tutsi feeling. Protesters demanding his dismissal marched on his offices on Friday, accusing him of being soft on Rwanda.
On Thursday, the transitional parliament called for Tutsis to be sacked from the army, civil service and state-run firms.
Demostrators have targeted cellular phone operator Telecel, one of Zaire's most successful companies. On Monday, its Tutsi chairman Miko Rwayitare resigned his post.
"The idea that Miko... and Telecel would be implicated in the political events that Zaire is going through today is completely absurd," said interim-chairman Joe Gatt.
